answer.evidence: The silhouette widens from 1 px at row 6 to 6 px at rows 10-14, then to 13 px at row 15. The column scans show thin vertical blade strokes (x=5, 9, 12) at rows 9-14, with pale tips at rows 9 and 10. Row 15 is a single light bluish line across the base. No horizontal plate, ellipse or band is drawn, so the sprite shows no top surface. It is a side view of upright tufts standing on a 1-row ground line, not a flat decal seen from above.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny sprite of a few frosty grass tufts, smaller than one 16x16 tile, on a flat dark grey backdrop. It is not a 4x3 ground patch, so it does not match the reference kind (grass and paving fields that fill the whole area). The facts show 5 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass reference. Tile-level tone counts are 0 because the piece is under one tile, so I judged by eye. By eye it has about 3 lightness steps, with no per-blade clumping, no soil grain and no tile-scale variation. The reference grass has about 3 visible tones per tile in mottled clumps, and the paving has stones shaded one by one. The 19% neutral share of dark edge pixels has little meaning here because there is almost no outline, only a few dark pixels at the base. The candidate is much thinner and sparser than either reference and would look like a sticker beside them, so it fails.
